correctness.rationale: A direct all-field proof normalizes any derivation modulo inner derivations to scalar geodesic edge weights. For odd cycles all shortest paths are unique; for even cycles the complete antipodal relations reduce to \(m+1\) independent constraints. Quotient by the \(n-1\) vertex gradients gives the claimed modules. In characteristic two an edge-fixed reflection acts on every lift of a fixed edge basis vector with nonzero kernel circulation, so the extension cannot split. Explicit symmetrization supplies the section outside characteristic two. The standalone checker verified finite examples for \(3\le n\le16\) over \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_3,\mathbb F_5,\mathbb F_7\). Finite checks supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: This supplies the intrinsic first Hochschild derivation module, complete dihedral symmetry, and a sharp characteristic-two nonsplitting phenomenon for an infinite natural family of shortest-path algebras. The even cycles are precisely the tope graphs of central rank-two line arrangements with that number of chambers; their mod-two magnitude-cohomology rings are actively studied, but the outer-derivation HH1 and its symmetry extension are distinct. The result explains a parity-and-characteristic boundary not visible from ordinary dimensions alone and offers a natural comparison for future algebraic studies.
